intro: 488 cells were tested across 34 instruments, 2016-10-24 to 2022-12-30. 387 pass Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.10, against about 24 expected by chance at p < 0.05. Most effects here are large, so the sweep is about where they bend, not whether they exist. The chosen lines exist only from 2020-08, and C.OG turbulent regimes come from just 16 distinct episodes (103 instrument spells, median 69 sessions).

Miss persistence holds across everything. Plain σ: yesterday's miss carries +0.49 into today, from 0.25 (USDCAD) to 0.68 (GBPAUD), in every year (0.34 in 2017 to 0.60 in 2020) and in both regimes (calm 0.47, turbulent 0.55). Indices persist most (0.60), majors and gold least (0.39). The chosen σ halves it to 0.25 and is flat across regimes, terciles and classes (0.21-0.28). log-HAR leaves 0.11. Benchmark: 0 (shuffled misses give ±0.02).

It holds within each London time bucket too: yesterday's Asia, open, mid and NY-afternoon misses each carry 0.36-0.40 into the same hours today on the plain σ (0.18-0.22 chosen). The overlap 13-16 persists least (plain 0.30, chosen 0.08): release-driven hours repeat less.

Big morning → big afternoon holds across all 34 instruments (slope 0.34 NZDCAD to 0.73 DE30; pooled 0.56 [0.52, 0.61]), every year (0.48-0.73) and both regimes (calm 0.56, turbulent 0.57). Against the chosen σ it is still 0.42, and the part of the morning not already in yesterday's miss still gives 0.45. It fades only slowly with horizon: 0.60 for 13-14, 0.57 for 16-22, 0.41 for the whole next session. Benchmark 0 = a random walk with σ right.

Error feedback pays everywhere on the plain σ (QLIKE 0.69 of plain; 0.84 majors to 0.64 indices; 0.59 in 2020). On the chosen σ the gain is smaller and local: 0.92 overall, 0.88 in the busy σ tercile vs 0.96 normal, 0.89 in 2022 vs 0.97 in 2021 (range crosses 1). It is not an alignment artefact: with every miss delayed one more session the gain shrinks (plain 0.81, chosen 0.96) but stays below 1, except gold on the chosen σ, which reverses to 1.04.

Plateau: no lone peak. The gain is a smooth monotone curve in the EWMA half-life, best at the shortest memory (plain 0.70 at 1 session, 0.96 at 55; chosen 0.91 to 0.97). Any half-life helps; shorter helps more.

Turning points: every forecast lags the rise. Over days −10 to +5 of a turbulent onset, misses run above each forecast's own calm-day level by +0.31 (plain), +0.35 (log-HAR), +0.26 (chosen, 8 episodes) and +0.12 (plain + error feedback). Afterwards the plain σ overshoots (−0.20 over days +6 to +60), log-HAR is level (+0.02) and the chosen σ stays slightly low (+0.08).

Coverage is honest on average but local by class and year: chosen p75 is crossed on 27.3% of FX-major sides, 21.0% gold, 18.2% UK100 and 20.5% DE30, 23.6% in 2021 and 28.0% in 2022. By regime it is too noisy to tell (calm 25.1%, turbulent 27.6% [23.9, 29.3]). First crossings land in the overlap 13-16 more than a random walk on each class's own clock says (34.7% vs about 30%), and less in Asia.

Decay monitors (C.OG Lesson 04): the plain-σ feedback gain is steady by half-year (0.67-0.77, 0.54 in 2020H1); the chosen-σ gain wobbles (0.87-1.01). The after-miss p75 gap on the plain lines grew from 10 points (2017) to 16-19 (2019-22); on the chosen lines it is 5-6 points. Costs fell rather than rose: spread as % of σ dropped for every class 2017 to 2022 (indices 3.3% to 0.8%, partly a data-feed change).

For the system: size and stops should use the chosen σ plus a short-memory miss term, widened after a hot day and after a hot morning, most of all on indices and GBP crosses. A stop at the chosen p75 is about 2 points too tight on majors and too loose on gold and European indices. Do not shrink a stop because the morning was wide. The days around a vol spike are when σ is most stale; the plain σ then runs too high for weeks.

charts.title: Does yesterday's miss carry into today? Persistence slope by regime, class and instrument
charts.unit: slope of today's RV miss on yesterday's
charts.note: Miss = log(5-minute RV ÷ calibrated σ²). Benchmark 0 = a forecast whose misses are independent (shuffled misses give ±0.02). All instruments: plain 0.4949 [0.456, 0.5327], chosen 0.2453 [0.1915, 0.291], log-HAR 0.1085 [0.0383, 0.1929]. Plain in calm 0.472 [0.428, 0.5142] vs turbulent 0.5453 [0.4679, 0.6148] (regime ranges use blocks of 69 sessions, the median spell). Look for rows where chosen drops toward 0: the chosen σ's own feedback term works there.

charts.title: How often the day goes past the p75 line, by regime, tercile, class, year and instrument (2020-08 to 2022)
charts.note: Benchmark 25% on every row (the line's own promise). Chosen in calm 25.0551% [23.876, 26.8055] vs turbulent 27.593% [23.9123, 29.2872] (regime ranges in blocks of 69 sessions; turbulent days in this window come from few episodes). Single instruments are about ±3.5 points of noise. Year rows show only the chosen value twice (no plain split). Above 25 = the line is too tight there, so a stop at it is hit more than planned.

charts.title: Persistence of the miss within each London time-of-day bucket (yesterday's same hours → today's)
charts.note: Each bucket's own 5-minute RV against σ² × its past-only share of the day. Benchmark 0 = independent misses. Plain σ 2017-22, chosen σ 2020-08..22, date-block 95% ranges. A bucket that sits well above the others is where yesterday's error is most worth feeding back.

charts.title: When the chosen p75 line is first crossed: share of crossings in each London time bucket
names: random walk on the data's own clock
charts.note: Chosen lines, OH and OL pooled, 2020-08..22. Benchmark: a random walk whose hourly variance follows each class's average hourly RV, with the day's vol off by sd 0.23 (stage 2), line set at its own p75; weighted by class. Real above benchmark = misses arrive in that bucket more than the clock alone says (scheduled releases, opens).

charts.title: Big morning → big afternoon: slope of the 13:00-22:00 RV miss on the 00:00-13:00 miss, by class and instrument
charts.note: Both misses against the plain σ² × each window's past-only share, 2017-22. Benchmark 0: if σ were right, a random walk's morning and afternoon variance are independent. All instruments 0.5637 [0.5186, 0.6093]; the part of the morning not already in yesterday's miss still gives 0.4468 [0.3996, 0.4975]; against the chosen σ (2020-08..22) 0.4158 [0.3562, 0.4693]. Classes and instruments with 95% date-block ranges.

charts.title: Morning surprise against what comes next, by horizon and C.OG regime
charts.note: Outcome = the RV miss over 13-14, 13-16, 16-22, 13-22 London, or the whole next session. Benchmark 0 (random walk with σ right). Turbulent rows rest on 16 distinct episodes; ranges (numbers.json) use blocks of 69 sessions. Look at whether the slope fades with horizon and whether turbulence steepens it.

charts.title: Where error feedback pays: QLIKE loss of σ + feedback ÷ the same σ without it
charts.note: Benchmark 1.0 = the forecast without the feedback term (below 1 = feedback helps). Plain: 2019-01-02 to 2022 (35,056 instrument-days). Chosen: 2021-01-04 to 2022 (16,171). Feedback = σ² × exp(b × yesterday's, 5-day and 22-day misses), b refit each January on earlier years; same past-only scale for both. Regime rows use blocks of 69 sessions. log-HAR ÷ plain overall: 0.7221.

charts.title: +1 lag check: the feedback gain with every miss delayed one more session
charts.note: Benchmark 1.0 = no feedback. Plain: 0.6945 [0.6328, 0.7525] → 0.813 [0.7442, 0.8742]. Chosen: 0.9191 [0.883, 0.967] → 0.9631 [0.9334, 0.997]. An alignment artefact would vanish with the extra delay; real persistence shrinks but stays below 1 because misses decay slowly (lag-2 autocorrelation 0.37 for plain).

charts.title: Plateau check: feedback gain against the half-life of the error memory
charts.note: One feature (an EWMA of past misses), b refit each January. Benchmark 1.0. A broad flat bottom = a plateau (the half-life does not need tuning); one sharp dip = a peak (fragile). Stage 2 used yesterday + 5-day + 22-day means, which spans roughly half-lives 1 to 15.

charts.title: Turning points: forecast σ against realised σ around the start of each turbulent episode
charts.unit: σ ÷ the σ of days −40 to −21
charts.note: 96 instrument onsets 2018-09..2022 in 14 distinct episodes (onsets within 60 days across instruments = one episode). Onset = first day of a C.OG turbulent spell (63-session vol > 1.25 × its past median for 21+ sessions). Benchmark: the realised line; the gap between a forecast and it is the lag. The chosen σ exists only from 2020-08: 49 of its onsets (8 episodes) are in the bars chart and the worked example.

charts.title: Lag and overshoot at turning points: each forecast's miss around a turbulent onset, beyond its usual calm-day miss
charts.note: Benchmark 0 = the forecast misses by no more than it does on an ordinary calm day (its own calm-day average is subtracted). Positive = forecast too low (lags the rise); negative = forecast too high (overshoots after the spike). Windows: before (−20 to −11), rise (−10 to +5), after (+6 to +60). 95% ranges resample whole episodes (14 plain-window episodes, 8 for chosen), because instruments in one episode move together.

charts.title: Decay monitor 1: rolling skill by half-year (QLIKE ratio)
charts.note: Benchmark 1.0 = no better than the denominator. C.OG's Lesson 04: an edge is a wasting asset, so watch whether the gain shrinks toward 1 over time. A line drifting up toward 1 is decay; a line that stays put is a stable effect. Half-years with fewer than 1,000 rows are skipped.

charts.title: Decay monitor 2: the response to the same conditioning variable, year by year

series.name: after-miss p75 hit gap ÷ 100, plain lines

charts.note: Benchmark 0 for every line. Persistence = slope of today's miss on yesterday's. Morning → afternoon = slope of the 13-22 miss on the 00-13 miss. After-miss gap = p75 hit rate after the top fifth of yesterday's misses minus after the bottom fifth (plain lines in-sample before 2020-08). Flat lines across years = a stable response; a falling line = the effect fading. 2020 for chosen is a part-year and is left out.

charts.title: Decay monitor 3: cost drift. Median bid/ask spread (07-16 London) as % of the day's σ
charts.note: From the M1 bid/ask closes, one spread per day. Benchmark: the class's own 2017 level (and the repo's feasibility gate, spread ÷ ATR 0.15, which is roughly 25% of σ). A rising line means a stop or target set in σ units costs more of its distance each year; falling = cheaper. σ = plain σ at the open.

charts.title: Worked example: GBPUSD around the turbulent onset of 2022-06-13
charts.note: Picked by rule: the chosen-window onset whose chosen σ ran furthest below realised over its first 20 sessions (mean miss 0.491). Benchmark: the realised line. All forecasts on the same past-only scale. Watch how many sessions each forecast takes to catch the rise, and whether it then overshoots the fall.
